senses.gloss: f. (טלל) cover, sheet, cloak (similar to the Roman pallium, Gr. φᾶρος).
units: <cite ref="Shabbat 147a:4">Sabb. 147ᵃ</cite> <he>ט׳ מקופלת</he> a cloak folded up and thrown over the shoulder.
<cite ref="Menachot 41a:8">Men. 41ᵃ</cite> <he>ט׳ כפולה</he> a double-sized sheet worn by doubling it.
<cite ref="Shabbat 138a:11">Sabb. 138ᵃ</cite> <he>ט׳ כפולה וכ׳</he> one must not make a tent on the Sabbath by spreading a double-sized sheet on poles so that the ends hang down.

Kidd. 18ᵃ sq. (ref. to בבגדו, Ex. XXI, 8) כיון שפירש טַלִּיתוֹ עליה since he spread his (bed-) sheet over her (v. בָּגַד).—Esp. Tallith, the cloak of honor, the scholar’s or officer’s distinction (adorned with fringes according to Num. XV, 38 sq.); the cloak of the leader in prayer.
Num. R. s. 8, end שמלה זו ט׳ simlah (Deut. X, 18), that means the cloak to which the show-fringes are attached.

<cite ref="Bereishit Rabbah 36:6">Gen. R. s. 36</cite> (ref. to <he>השמלה</he>, <cite ref="Genesis 9:23">Gen. IX, 23</cite>) <he>לפיכך זכה שם לט׳ וכ׳</he> therefore was Shem privileged to wear the Tallith &c.
Ex. R. s. 27 נתמנה … ונטל ט׳ וכ׳ when one has been appointed to an office and has taken the T., he must not &c.; a. fr.—Pl. טַלִּיתוֹת, טַלִּיּוֹת.

<cite ref="Shabbat 147a:1">Sabb. 147ᵃ</cite> ed. (Ms. M. sing.). Tanḥ. Korah 2; <cite ref="Bamidbar Rabbah 18:3">Num. R. s. 18</cite>, beg. <he>ט׳ תכלת</he> cloaks all of purple blue; <cite ref="Jerusalem Talmud Sanhedrin 10:1:17">Y. Snh. X, 27ᵈ</cite> bot. <he>טלויות</he>, ed. Krot. <he>טלוי׳</he> (corr. acc. or <cite ref="I00497"><he>טַלִּיוֹת</he></cite>).
<cite ref="Mishnah Zavim 4:5">Zab. IV, 5</cite> <he>עשר טליות וכ׳</he> if ten sheets are placed above one another.
